entries.meaning: Rainbow
entries.note: Also associated with the iris flower and the coloured part of the eye.

entries.meaning: He will laugh
My God is an oath
entries.note: A Latinate form of Isabel, from Elizabeth.

entries.meaning: A name from the island of Islay
entries.note: Also spelled like the Spanish word for island; the Scottish name has a different pronunciation.

entries.meaning: The ivy plant

From Welsh, Spanish, Portuguese, and Galician Iago, from Latin Iācōbus (“James”), from Ancient Greek Ἰάκωβος (Iákōbos), from Hebrew יַעֲקֹב (ya‘ăqṓḇ, “Jacob”, literally “he will/shall heel”), from עָקֵב (‘āqḗḇ, “heel”) and the Biblical account of the patriarch Jacob's birth in Genesis 25:26. Doublet of Yago, Jago, James, Jacob, Jacques, and Santiago.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: From Scottish Gaelic. Cognate of John; see there for more.
entries.note: A male given name from Scottish Gaelic, equivalent to English John.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Latin Iamblichus, from Koine Greek Ἰάμβλιχος (Iámblikhos), from Aramaic ימלכו (Yamlīḵū), perhaps originally a causative form of the verb מלך (mlk, “to rule”).
entries.note: A male given name from Koine Greek, of historical usage.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Scottish Gaelic Eòin.
entries.note: A male given name from Scottish Gaelic Eòin, equivalent to English John.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit इच्छा (icchā, “desire, will, wish”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From Biblical Hebrew אִיכָבוֹד (ʾīḵāḇōḏ, literally “no honor”), from אִי (ʾī, “not”) + כָּבוֹד (kāḇōḏ, “honor”); alluding to 1 Samuel 4:21, where Eli’s daughter-in-law names her child Ichabod, saying ‘The glory is departed from Israel.’
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese いちろう (Ichirō), a given name with numerous possible original kanji.
entries.note: A male given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: Variant of Hick, a medieval diminutive of Richard.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: From Sanskrit इडा (iḍā).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Latin Idaeus, from Ancient Greek Ἰδαῖος (Idaîos).
entries.note: A male given name from Latin [in turn from Ancient Greek], of historical usage

entries.meaning: From the medieval male (and less often female) given name Ida.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Latin Idomeneus, from Ancient Greek Ἰδομενεύς (Idomeneús).
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Welsh Idris.
entries.note: A male given name from Welsh, popularized by actor Idris Elba.

entries.meaning: American 20th-century phonetic spelling of Aisha.
entries.note: A female given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: American 20th-century phonetic spelling of Aisha.
entries.note: A female given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Clipping + -y.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Ignatius.

entries.meaning: From Latin Ignātius, variant of gens name Egnātius, altered to resemble ignis (“fire”), establishing a folk etymology meaning akin to “Fiery One”. Of uncertain origin, perhaps originally borrowed from Etruscan.
entries.note: A male given name from Latin; of mostly Roman Catholic or Eastern Orthodox usage in English.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Russian Игна́тий (Ignátij), from Latin Ignātius.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Russian male given name Игна́тий (Ignátij).

entries.meaning: Transliterated from Russian И́горь (Ígorʹ), a Varangian name derived from Old Norse Yngvarr, Ingvarr, from Yngvi (name of a god) + herr (“army”). Doublet of Ivor, Ihar, and Ihor.
entries.note: A male given name from Russian.

entries.meaning: From Hindi [Term?], from Sanskrit [Term?] Iha (world or earth) and 'Hitha' ("who does Good, favor").
entries.note: A female given name from Hindi used in India, meaning a goddess who does good for all creatures in the world.

entries.meaning: Apparently an elaboration of James.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: From Igbo ijèọma (“good journey, safe journey (general); good journey in life”).
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit इक्ष्वाकु (ikṣvāku).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese いくこ (Ikuko).
entries.note: A female given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese いくみ (Ikumi).
entries.note: A female given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit इला (ilā).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From Hebrew אִילָן (Ilán, “tree, oak tree”).
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Ukrainian Іларіон (Ilarion), Russian Иларион (Ilarion).
entries.note: A male given name from Russian, Ukrainian

entries.meaning: From Arabic إِلْهَام (ʔilhām).
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Three possible origins: * A matronymic surname from the Middle English personal name Ayleve, which is from Old English Ǣþelġifu; this name is composed of the elements ǣþel (“noble”) and ġiefu (“gift, present”). * From the Old Norse personal name Eilif, which is composed of the elements ei (“always”) and líf (“life”).
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: From Ukrainian Ілля́ (Illjá). Compare Russian Илья́ (Ilʹjá) and Belarusian Ілья́ (Ilʹjá).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Ukrainian male given name Ілля́ (Illjá)

entries.meaning: From Hungarian Ilona. A rare variant of Helen or Helena.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: From Russian Илья́ (Ilʹjá). Doublet of Elijah.
entries.note: A male given name from Russian.

entries.meaning: See iman.
entries.note: A unisex given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic إيمان (ʔīmān).
entries.note: A unisex given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Persian ایمانقلی (imânqoli), from Old Anatolian Turkish.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Persian male given name ایمانقلی (imânqoli)

entries.meaning: From Romance (Italian Imelda, Spanish Imelda), from German Irmhild.
entries.note: A female given name from the Romance languages.

entries.meaning: From Egyptian jj-m-ḥtp (literally “(the one) coming in peace, (the one) returning home safely”): M18-G17-R4:X1*Q3 from the perfective active participle of jj (“to come, to return”) + m ḥtp (“in peace, safely”).
entries.note: A male given name from Egyptian.

entries.meaning: From Hebrew עִמָּנוּאֵל (ʿimanuʾél), from עִמָּנוּ אֵל (ʿimánu ʾél, literally “God is with us”).
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew: alternative form of Emmanuel.

entries.meaning: First used by William Shakespeare in Cymbeline, a misprint for Innogen, from Scottish Gaelic inghean (“girl, maiden”)
entries.note: A female given name from the Celtic languages.

entries.meaning: Non-standard spelling of Imogen.
entries.note: A female given name from the Celtic languages.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Manipuri ꯏꯃꯣꯏꯅꯨ (ʼimoʼinu).
entries.note: A female given name from Manipuri.

entries.meaning: Patronymic surname from an unclear personal name.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: From Arabic عِمْرَان (ʕimrān).
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Hebrew אִמְרִי (Imri).
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic إِمْتِنَان (ʔimtinān, “gratitude”).
entries.note: A unisex given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Short form of given names ending in -ina, e.g. Georgina, Christina, Wilhelmina.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Calque of Hebrew יוֹסֵף. From increase.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: From Indian + -a. From Indiana Territory, dating from 1800, noting the territory's large Native American Indian population. From Indian Territory.
entries.note: A placename. A ghost town in Haldimand County, Ontario, Canada.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit इन्दिरा (indirā).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit commonly used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit इंद्रनील (iṃdranīla).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit इंद्राणी (iṃdrāṇī).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit इंद्रनील (iṃdranīla).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From Russian Ине́сса (Inéssa).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Russian female given name Инесса (Inessa)

entries.meaning: Anglicised form of Spanish Inés and Portuguese Inês, both from Latin Agnes, from Ancient Greek Ἁγνή (Hagnḗ). First used in 18th century English poetry and plays referring to Inês de Castro. Doublet of Agnes.
entries.note: A female given name from Spanish.

entries.meaning: From Danish, Norwegian, Swedish Inga etc., all from Old Norse Inga.
entries.note: A female given name from Old Norse.

entries.meaning: From a Middle English given name, from Proto-Germanic *Ingwaz (“a Germanic god”) + *hrabnaz (“raven”). The places are named after persons with the surname.
entries.note: A male given name from the Germanic languages, in modern use transferred back from the surname.

entries.meaning: From Swedish, Norwegian and Danish Ingrid, from Old Norse Ingiríðr.
entries.note: A female given name from Old Norse.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Russian И́нна (Ínna), of uncertain origin. (One suggestion is Ancient Greek ἴννα (ínna), from ἴννην (ínnēn, “little girl”).)
entries.note: A transliteration of the Belarusian or Russian female given name И́нна (Ínna).

entries.meaning: Derived from Scottish Gaelic inghean (“girl, maiden”).
entries.note: A female given name from the Celtic languages.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Greek Ιωάννης (Ioánnis), a male given name used in (modern) Greece. Doublet of Giannis.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Greek male given name Ιωάννης (Ioánnis).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἴον (íon, “violet”), evoking the flower's symbolism of modesty and beauty.
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: From Koine Greek ἰόλη (iólē, “violet”) + ἄνθος (ánthos, “flower”). Cognate with French Yolande, Italian Iolanda, Spanish Yolanda.
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: Probably a misreading of Latin Ioua, an attempt to Latinize Old Irish Í.
entries.note: A female given name transferred from the place name, of mostly Scottish usage.

entries.meaning: From Arabic إِقْبَال (ʔiqbāl).
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic

entries.meaning: From a Hebrew name עִירָא ('ira), from a word meaning "watchful".
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew, mostly of American usage.

entries.meaning: From Georgian ირაკლი (iraḳli), ultimately from Ancient Greek Ἡρακλῆς (Hēraklês).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Georgian male given name ირაკლი (iraḳli), equivalent to Heracles.

entries.meaning: From Latin Īrēnaeus, from Ancient Greek Εἰρηναῖος (Eirēnaîos), from εἰρήνη (eirḗnē, “peace”).
entries.note: A male given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from French Irène, from Ancient Greek Εἰρήνη (Eirḗnē, “peace”), name of a goddess of peace, of early Christian saints, and of an 8th-century Byzantine empress. Doublet of Eirini.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek, in regular use since the 19th century.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic عِرْفَان (ʕirfān, “knowledge”). This given name is mostly found in Pakistan.
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: From Russian Ири́на (Irína), akin to English Irene.
entries.note: A female given name from Russian.

entries.meaning: From Middle English Irish (12th c.), from Old English *Īrisċ, from Old English Īras (“Irishmen”), from Old Norse Írar, from Old Irish Ériu (modern Irish Éire (“Ireland”)), further origin heavily debated but probably from Proto-Celtic *Φīweriyū (“fat land, fertile”), from Proto-Indo-European *péyh₂wr̥ (“fat, swelling”), from *peyh₂- (“to swell; to be fat”), akin to Ancient Greek πῑ́ειρα (pī́eira, “fertile land”), Sans…
entries.note: A female given name of chiefly Philippine usage.

entries.meaning: From German Irma in the nineteenth century. Short form of Germanic names beginning with irm(en)-, erm(en) "whole, entire", from Proto-Germanic *ermunaz. Cognate with English Emma.
entries.note: A female given name from the Germanic languages.

entries.meaning: Shortening.
entries.note: A male given name. Clipping of Irvin.

entries.meaning: Probably from Celtic words cognate with Welsh ir, yr (“green, fresh”) + afon (“water”).
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname.

entries.meaning: Variant of the Scottish habitational surname Irvine, probably from a Celtic word cognate with Welsh ir, yr (“fresh”) + afon (“river”).
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname, often used by English-speaking Jews to anglicize Israel.

entries.meaning: From a medieval given name Erwin, from Eoforwine, from Old English eofor (“boar”) + wine (“friend”), the latter of which is from Proto-West Germanic *wini.
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname.

entries.meaning: From Belarusian and Ukrainian Іри́на (Irýna), akin to English Irene.
entries.note: A female given name from Ukrainian or Belarusian.

entries.meaning: From Isabel, Isabella and Isabelle.
entries.note: A diminutive of the female given name Isabel or of its variant forms, sometimes also used as a formal given name.

entries.meaning: A rare spelling variant of Isaac.
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Variant of Isaacs.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: From Spanish Isabel, from Old Occitan Elisabel, from Latin Elisabeth, from Ancient Greek Ἐλισάβετ (Elisábet), from Hebrew אֱלִישֶׁבַע (Elishéva, “my God is an oath”). Doublet of Elizabeth.
entries.note: A female given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Spanish Isabela. The province is named after Isabella II of Spain. Doublet of Isabelle.
entries.note: A female given name from Spanish.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from French Isabelle.
entries.note: A female given name from French Isabelle, ultimately a variant of Elizabeth.

entries.meaning: From Isabel /Isabella /Isabelle + -ia.
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: A non-standard variant of Isidore, possibly inspired by the well-known feminine variant Isadora of Isidora.
entries.note: A male given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: From Ancient Greek Ἠσαΐας (Ēsaḯas) from Hebrew יְשַׁעְיָהוּ (yəšaʿyā́hū).
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: From Arabic عِصَام (ʕiṣām, “security, pledge”).
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Old French, the name of the queen who fell in love with Tristan in medieval romance Tristan and Iseult, perhaps from Celtic, of uncertain meaning, possibly Proto-Brythonic *Adsiltia (“she who is gazed upon”); compare Welsh syllu and Irish súil. Otherwise from Germanic, equivalent to Old High German is (“ice”) + hiltja (“battle”) (from Proto-West Germanic *hildi).
entries.note: A female given name from the Germanic languages.

entries.meaning: Shortening.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Ishmael.

entries.meaning: From Sanskrit ईशान (īśāna, “Ishana”), a Hindu deity and guardian of the northeast direction.
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit, of Indian origin.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic إِسْحَاق (ʔisḥāq). Doublet of Isaac.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Rendering of Scottish Gaelic Isbeal, short form of Iseabail (“Isabel”).
entries.note: A female given name from Scottish Gaelic.

entries.meaning: From Hebrew יִשְׁמָעֵאל (yishma'él (yišmāʿēl), “God hears, God will hear”). Doublet of Ismail.
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Name of a fourth-century saint. The feminine equivalent of Isidore, from Ancient Greek Ἰσιδώρα (Isidṓra, “gift of Isis”).
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek; rare in the Anglo-Saxon world.

entries.meaning: French form of the name of early Spanish saints, from Ancient Greek Ἰσίδωρος (Isídōros), meaning "gift of (the goddess) Isis".
entries.note: A male given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: Learned borrowing from Latin Īsis from Ancient Greek Ἶσις (Îsis), from Egyptian st-t:H8-B1 (ꜣst).
entries.note: A female given name from Egyptian or Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic الْإِسْكَنْدَر (al-ʔiskandar, “Alexander”). Doublet of Alexander
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic [in turn from Ancient Greek], variant of Alexander; variant forms Askandar, Askander, Eskandar, Eskender, Eskinder, Iskander, Iskinder, Scandar, Scander, Sikandar, Sikander, Skandar, Skander.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic الإسْكَنْدَر (al-ʔiskandar, “Alexander”). This surname is mostly found among Copts in Egypt. Doublet of Alexander
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic [in turn from Ancient Greek], variant of Iskandar and Alexander.

entries.meaning: Clipping.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given names Ismael and Ismail.

entries.meaning: From Arabic إِسْمَاعِيل (ʔismāʕīl). Doublet of Ishmael.
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Matronymic surname from a somewhat rare female given name found in the 13ᵗʰ century.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: From Ancient Greek Ἰσμήνη (Ismḗnē).
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek. A daughter and half-sister of Oedipus, daughter and granddaughter of Jocasta, and sister of Antigone, Eteocles and Polynices.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from the German Isolde, German form of Iseult.
entries.note: A female given name from the Celtic languages or the Germanic languages.
entries.origin: the Celtic languages or the Germanic languages

entries.meaning: From Middle English Israel, from Old English, borrowed from Latin Israel, from Ancient Greek Ἰσραήλ (Israḗl), from Hebrew יִשְׂרָאֵל (yisra'él, “Israel”). In the Bible, it is said to be from the name יִשְׂרֶה אֵל (yisré 'él) given to Jacob in Genesis 32:29, after which his descendants came to be known as Israelites and their land as the "kingdom/land of Israel".
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: From Arabic عيسى (“Jesus”).
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Old variant of Isaac.
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: From Biblical Hebrew יִשָּׂשכָר (“Issachar”), a son of Jacob.
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: From Japanese. The automotive manufacturer is named after the 五十鈴川 (Isuzu-gawa, “Isuzu River”).
entries.note: A female given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Hopi.
entries.note: A female given name from Hopi.

entries.meaning: Borrowing from Hebrew יצחק.
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew, variant of Isaac.

entries.meaning: Rare variant of Evan, from Welsh Ifan, the Welsh equivalent of John.
entries.note: A male given name from Welsh of Welsh origin.

entries.meaning: From various Slavic languages, such as Bulgarian, Macedonian, and Russian Ивана (Ivana). Doublet of Jana, Jane, Janice, Janis, Jean, Jeanne, Jen, Joan, Joanna, Joanne, Johanna, Juana, Shavonne, Sian, Siobhan, Shane, Shaun, Shauna, and Sheena.
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: From Czech Ivanka (from Ivana + -ka, q.v.). Doublet of Jan, Janelle, Janet, Janey, Janine, Jeanette, Jeanie, Jeannette, Jeannine, Jen, Jenna, Jenny, Jessie, Jo, Jody, Juanita, Shanae, Sinead, and Vanna.
entries.note: A female given name from Czech.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Ukrainian Іва́нна (Ivánna). Doublet of Jane.
entries.note: A female given name from Ukrainian.

entries.meaning: Clipping of Ivy
entries.note: A diminutive of the female given name Ivy.

entries.meaning: From the personal name Ives + -son.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: Latinate form of a medieval name of Old French origin, from Proto-Germanic *īhwaz (“yew, bow”). Name of French and English saints. Cognate with modern French Yves.
entries.note: A male given name from the Germanic languages.

entries.meaning: Medieval form of Old Norse Ívarr. Doublet of Igor.
entries.note: A male given name from Old Norse.

entries.meaning: The surname is habitational from Ivry in Normandy, and in some cases patronymic from a diminutive of Ivor. The modern given name is associated with ivory.
entries.note: A male given name from English.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese いわお (Iwao).
entries.note: A male given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: Rare spelling of Isaiah.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: From Ukrainian Ізя́слав (Izjáslav).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Ukrainian male given name Ізясла́в (Izjasláv)

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese 泉 (izumi, “spring; fountain”).
entries.note: A female given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: From the /ɪz-/ root of the names + -ie.
entries.note: Alternative spelling of Izzy (diminutive of female and male given names)

entries.meaning: From the /ɪz-/ root of the names + -y. The common noun derives from Isaac and Israel, male given names of Hebrew origin, popular among Jewish people, the latter also being the name of the self-defined Jewish state.
entries.note: A diminutive of the female given name Isabel, Isobel, Isabelle, Isabella, Elizabeth, Isidora, Isra, Izebel, Ismara and Isobelle.
